defects.description: nginx-proxy.depends_on names service `flask`, but the application service is named `flask-app`; there is no service `flask`.
paraphrases: The proxy depends on `flask`, but the service is `flask-app`.
defects.rationale: Findable by cross-checking depends_on against the service list; the app service is `flask-app`.

defects.description: The proxy targets FLASK_SERVER_ADDR=flask-app:9000, but the flask-app service publishes port 8000, so the proxy points at the wrong port.
paraphrases: The proxy sends traffic to flask-app:9000, but flask-app is on port 8000.
FLASK_SERVER_ADDR should use port 8000 to match the flask-app service.
The upstream port the proxy dials (9000) is not one flask-app serves.
defects.rationale: Findable by comparing FLASK_SERVER_ADDR (line 8) with the flask-app ports (line 23); should be 8000.

defects.description: The flask-app runs gunicorn bound to 0.0.0.0:5000, but the service publishes port 8000 and its healthcheck probes 8000, so nothing is actually served on the exposed port.
paraphrases: gunicorn binds :5000 while the service exposes and health-checks :8000.
gunicorn's internal listener is on :5000, not the :8000 the compose file publishes and health-checks.
The application listens on the wrong port relative to what is published.
defects.rationale: Findable by comparing the gunicorn bind (line 29) with the ports and healthcheck (lines 23, 25); should be 8000.
